title: Koreans say "no jam" when it's boring 🍓 노잼 vs 꿀잼 #learnkorean
caption:
잼 (jaem) here is NOT jam. It's short for 재미 (jae-mi) = fun.

노잼 (no-jaem) = no + fun → boring
꿀잼 (kkul-jaem) = honey + fun → super fun (꿀 = honey)

Try it:
이 영화 노잼이야. (i yeong-hwa no-jaem-i-ya) — This movie is boring.
이 영화 꿀잼이야! (i yeong-hwa kkul-jaem-i-ya) — This movie is so fun!

Both are casual slang for friends — not for your boss or professor.

pinnedComment: Your last 노잼 movie? 👇 (and your last 꿀잼 one!)
alt: A needle-felted living room at night. A felt girl yawns at a dull TV and says 노잼… (no-jaem). The coral felt mascot Mongle hears "jam" and brings a jar of strawberry jam on its head. On screen: 잼 ≠ jam, 잼 = fun (short for 재미), 노 + 잼 = boring. Mongle sags and the girl pats it. Then the TV explodes into a car chase and she cheers 우와! 꿀잼! (kkul-jaem). Mongle thinks 꿀… 잼?! and comes back with a tray carrying a honey pot and the jam jar, tipping the honey all over the sofa. 꿀 = honey, 꿀잼 = super fun. The girl freezes: 내 소파… (my sofa…). The movie: 꿀잼. The sofa: 노잼…
